changesProposed.name: Breakthrough Energy

verified.name: Breakthrough Energy
verified.thesis: Breakthrough Energy invests in clean energy innovation across five sectors of the global economy that drive emissions. The firm invests primarily in businesses where the risk of failure is high and the timeframe for return on investment is 20 years. Clean technologies must be affordable and reliable to reach global scale.
verified.notes: In March 2025, Bill Gates dissolved the European unit and U.S. public policy unit. Strategy shifted away from public policy towards supporting clean energy technology through the Breakthrough Energy Catalyst program and Breakthrough Energy Ventures. Sources provided do not contain verified AUM, current senior partners beyond Bill Gates, or specific flagship fund AUM figures.

changesProposed.name: Engine Ventures

verified.name: Engine Ventures
verified.thesis: Engine Ventures invests in early-stage deep tech companies developing hardware-based technologies across fields including biotech, robotics, green energy, agriculture, manufacturing, material science, and quantum computing.
verified.notes: Engine Ventures spun out as a separate investment firm from The Engine (nonprofit incubator/accelerator) in 2023. The Engine was founded by MIT in 2016. Source [0] identifies 'Engine Ventures' as a distinct entity from 'The Engine' on the website. Source [1] states: 'In 2023, Engine Ventures spun out as a separate investment firm focused on Tough Tech companies.' Wikipedia [3] confirms: 'In 2023, the investment fund separated from The Engine and rebranded as the venture capital firm Engine Ventures.' No current senior partners of Engine Ventures are explicitly named in sources; Emily Knight is CEO/President of The Engine nonprofit, not Engine Ventures. No AUM figure found for Engine Ventures specifically. No flagship fund name verified. Source [4] is unrelated to Engine Ventures.
